stem: Which one of the following books was written by Tilak?
expl: The book “Gita Rahasya” was written by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak in Mandalay Jail. In it, he gave a detailed explanation of the Karma Yoga of the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita. After reading “Gita Rahasya,” Gandhiji said that Tilak’s commentary on the Gita would remain his eternal memorial. In the preface of this book, Tilak wrote: “I prepared the first draft of the book in Mandalay Jail during the winter of 1910–1911. Thereafter, as new ideas came to my mind, I kept improving that draft from time to time, and the parts that had to be left incomplete due to the lack of necessary books were completed after my release from prison.” This makes it clear that most of “Gita Rahasya” was written by Tilak in Mandalay Jail itself, and some part was written after his release.

stem: Who had translated the Bengali play, Nil Darpan into English?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Dinabandhu Mitra’s Bengali play Nil Darpan mentions the Indigo Revolt (1859–60) and highlights the exploitation of peasants. The English translation of Nil Darpan from the original Bengali was published in 1861 without naming the translator, and the translator was mentioned only as “A Native” (as written in the original text—“Translated from the Bengali by a Native”). James Long, who published and supervised the English edition, never revealed the translator’s identity. Contemporary scholars like Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and Shibnath Shastri believed that the translator was Michael Madhusudan Dutt. Although this belief is widespread, there has been no formal confirmation. It remains a matter of controversy even today.

stem: Who founded the ‘Amrita Bazar Patrika’?
expl: The Amrita Bazar Patrika was founded by Motilal Ghosh and Shishir Kumar Ghosh in 1868 in Amrita Bazar village (now in Jessore district, Bangladesh). However, due to an epidemic in the village, its office was shifted to Calcutta in 1871. Initially, it was published in the Bengali language. To escape the Vernacular Press Act, 1878, the newspaper was converted overnight into an English-language publication. Girish Chandra Ghosh started The Bengalee in 1862, which was taken over by S.N. Banerjee in 1879.
